items.title: HYPERSPECTRAL IMAGING IN FRUIT QUALITY ASSESSMENT: SPECTRAL ANALYSIS, MACHINE LEARNING AND APPLICATIONS
items.abstract: Fruit quality assessment is important for maintaining postharvest quality, reducing losses and improving the efficiency of sorting and grading operations. Conventional destructive methods provide reliable measurements of physicochemical, chemical, mechanical and microbiological attributes, but generally require sample preparation, laboratory analysis and destruction of the fruit. Non-destructive techniques such as visual inspection, machine vision, near-infrared spectroscopy, multispectral imaging, thermal imaging and electronic nose systems have been increasingly used for fruit quality evaluation, although their ability to provide detailed spatial and spectral information simultaneously is limited. Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) combines imaging and spectroscopy to acquire spatially resolved spectral information from intact fruits, allowing both internal quality attributes and external defects to be assessed. This review discusses the development and working principles of HSI, scanning and illumination modes, and the major steps involved in spectral data processing, including preprocessing, feature extraction, wavelength selection and dimensionality reduction. Applications of HSI for internal quality attributes such as soluble solids content, pH, firmness and total soluble solids, as well as external defects and fungal diseases, are reviewed with emphasis on spectral range, data analysis methods and machine-learning models. The major challenges include limited and cultivar-specific datasets, environmental variability, laboratory-to-field transferability, insufficient external validation, high-dimensional data and the lack of standardized protocols. Future research should focus on compact and portable HSI systems, real-time inspection, artificial intelligence, multimodal sensing, transfer learning, standardized datasets and commercial-scale validation to support reliable and practical fruit quality assessment.

items.title: Identification of adventitious lung sounds in children with respiratory illnesses in Bangladesh using artificial intelligence and digital auscultation
items.abstract: Integrated management of childhood illness (IMCI) guidelines have high sensitivity but low specificity for pneumonia diagnosis. Artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled digital stethoscopes capable of analysing lung sounds may improve IMCI diagnostic performance. We evaluated the performance of an AI algorithm trained to identify normal and adventitious lung sounds in children. Non-physician health workers recorded lung sounds from four chest positions using a digital stethoscope in under-five-year-old children with suspected pneumonia at community clinics in Bangladesh. A trained paediatrician listening panel classified chest position recordings as normal, abnormal (crackles and/or wheeze), or uninterpretable. The AI algorithm similarly classified chest position recordings except for the uninterpretable category. AI algorithm and listening panel comparisons were made at the child-level, and included chest positions considered interpretable, uninterpretable, and high- and low-confidence by the panel. Of 990 enrolled children, 867 (87.6%) had at least 3 interpretable chest position recordings by the panel and were analysed. Compared to the panel, the AI algorithm’s sensitivity and specificity for detecting abnormal sounds were 61.8% and 60.7% among all children, and 63.5% and 66.8% in IMCI pneumonia cases. Overall, the AI algorithm achieved moderate classification performance. Classification performance will benefit from further AI algorithm training to categorize recordings as uninterpretable.

items.title: IMMEDIATE AFFECT OF EXAMINATION REALATED STATIC POSTURE OVER MUSCULOSKELETAL SYSTEM
items.abstract: Background: Examination periods require students to maintain prolonged static postures while sitting, reading, and writing continuously for extended durations.Such postural demands, combined with limited movement opportunities, may contribute to musculoskeletal discomfort and pain.However, limited evidence is available regarding the immediate musculoskeletal effects of examination-related static posture among college students.Objective: To investigate the immediate effect of examination-related static posture on the musculoskeletal system and to identify the prevalence and characteristics of post-examination musculoskeletal discomfort among college students.Methodology: An observational cross-sectional survey study was conducted among 350 college students aged 17-45 years who appeared for written examinations lasting at least one hour.Data were collected immediately after examinations using a self-structured questionnaire.Information regarding demographic characteristics, postural habits, ergonomic factors, examination-related stress, uniform-related discomfort, and musculoskeletal symptoms was obtained.Pain intensity was assessed using the Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS).Data were analysed using descriptive statistics and presented as frequencies and percentages.Results: Among the participants, 88.6% reported sitting continuously for at least one hour during examinations, 80.9% leaned forward while writing, and 65.1% maintained prolonged neck flexion.Examination-related stress was reported by 80% of students.Immediate post-examination musculoskeletal pain was reported by 65.1% of participants.Pain most commonly developed after the examination (52.9%) and was predominantly intermittent in nature (74.6%).Pain disturbed concentration in 66.0% of participants and affected sleep in 57.4%.Although 82.3% reported symptom relief after rest, 54.0% stated that discomfort persisted even after reaching home.Additional observations indicated recurrent musculoskeletal symptoms among students who completed the questionnaire following multiple examination sessions.Conclusion: Examination-related static posture is associated with a high prevalence of immediate musculoskeletal discomfort among college students.Prolonged continuous sitting, forward leaning posture while writing, sustained neck flexion, and examination-related stress emerged as the major contributing factors associated with post-examination musculoskeletal pain.The findings emphasize the importance of ergonomic awareness, proper sitting posture, regular postural adjustments, and appropriate examination seating arrangements to reduce musculoskeletal discomfort and promote students' well-being and academic performance.

items.title: Impacts of heterogeneous unmanned vehicle combinations on task performance and workload: A visual behavioral perspective
items.abstract: Heterogeneous unmanned vehicles system, comprising Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) and Unmanned Ground Vehicles (UGVs), offer complementary advantages in Search and Rescue missions. However, the impact of different vehicle combinations on operator remains unclear. This study investigated how unmanned vehicle combinations (1UAV+3UGV, 2UAV+2UGV, and 3UAV+1UGV) influence operator performance and workload in Search and Rescue scenario. Thirty-six participants performed the simulated missions. The results indicate that the balanced 2UAV+2UGV combination leads to higher performance and lower workload. To identify underlying mechanisms, participants were grouped by median performance and workload. High-performance participants exhibited a more proactive and efficient information acquisition strategy, flexibly allocating attention through more frequent saccades and fixation transitions between critical areas. Additionally, higher perceived workload was associated with a video-centric attention pattern that may reflect visual tunneling and limit the acquisition of global mission information. This research integrates vehicle combination and cognitive mechanisms to inform the design of heterogeneous unmanned systems.

items.title: Impacts of Occupational Health and Safety Hazards on Quality of Work life in Food Industry of Pakistan
items.abstract: The impact of Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) hazards on the Quality of Work Life (QWL) of the employees of the food industry in Pakistan has been studied. Food manufacturing operations are often dangerous, and workers are likely to be exposed to physical, chemical, biological, ergonomic, psychological, mechanical and electrical hazards. A quantitative research method was followed with a cross-sectional survey design, and 121 total employees of food processing organisations of Pakistan participated in the study to collect data across the various departments of these food processing organisations. The relationships between OHS hazards and QWL were analyzed by using SPSS using correlation and multiple regression analyses. The results indicate that the chemical and ergonomic hazards are the most important factors influencing QWL, followed by psychological hazards, physical hazards, mechanical hazards and electrical hazards, with biological hazards not being statistically significant. The findings reflect the multi-faceted impact of work safety on employees' wellbeing, satisfaction, and work-life balance. This study adds to the very few studies conducted on the OHS of food industry workers in Pakistan and offers implications for improving worksite safety, optimizing worker health, and improving organizational productivity.

items.title: Implementing AI and Virtual Reality in Elite Sports Psychology
items.abstract: In team sports, psychological regulation is crucial, yet traditional methods lack personalization, rely on subjective assessments, and offer low realism. This study examined the integration of computer-assisted technologies into psychological training. A six-month trial involved 90 professional football, basketball, and ice hockey players, randomly assigned to an experimental group or control group. Data on physiology, psychology, performance, and team communication were analyzed using t-tests. Per the results, the experimental group showed 21.3% lower anxiety, 25.4% higher cohesion, 21.2% faster decision response, 14.3% higher clutch success, 38.7% better communication efficiency; clutch error rate was also reduced from 27% to 11%. However, ~15% experienced virtual reality discomfort, and artificial intelligence overreliance reduced tactical creativity by 19%. Computer-assisted technologies enhance psychological resilience and team performance. Balancing data-driven precision with human-centered coaching is vital. Future work should optimize training models and establish data ethics.

items.title: Improving Postpolypectomy Surveillance Decisions Using an Automated Analysis of Colonoscopy and Histopathology Reports: 2-Center Validation Study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Postpolypectomy surveillance intervals derived from colonoscopy findings and histopathology should be guideline-based, yet these are frequently not adhered to, contributing to under- and oversurveillance. This motivates a more structured and automated approach to improve adherence. Objective We developed and evaluated an automated, implementable, guideline-aligned decision support tool that extracts colorectal polyp features from free-text colonoscopy and histopathology reports and produces auditable surveillance recommendations. Methods We extracted paired colonoscopy and histopathology reports from a National Health Service (NHS) trust and designed a 4-stage prompting pipeline using open-weight large language models to separate multispecimen histopathology reports into individual containers (“pots”), align endoscopic findings with specimens, and normalize each pot into a structured schema. The surveillance intervals were then computed by a deterministic rule engine encoding guideline rules. We evaluated extraction performance on 100 procedures (215 pots), assessed surveillance recommendation performance on a same-site cohort (n=100), and performed external validation on a cohort from a second trust (n=100). A separate retrospective audit compared automated recommendations and observed routine scheduling against a clinician-derived reference based on full electronic health record review in 127 patients. Results Key extraction fields showed end-to-end accuracy (specimen type=0.995; location=0.981; diagnosis=0.981; excision completeness=0.949), with mean report-level pot comprehensiveness of 0.968 (SD 0.112). Overall surveillance recommendation accuracy was 0.96 (95% CI 0.90-0.98) at Guy’s and St Thomas’ NHS Foundation Trust (GSTT) and 0.93 (95% CI 0.86-0.97) at Sandwell and West Birmingham NHS Trust (SWB) and showed strong class-level performance ( no follow-up F 1 -score of 0.98 at GSTT and 0.97 at SWB; site check F 1 -score of 0.93 at GSTT and 0.91 at SWB; 3-year follow-up F 1 -score of 0.86 at GSTT and 0.80 at SWB; cancer alert F 1 -score of 1.00 at GSTT and 1.00 at SWB). The comparison to current clinical practice showed that the tool would improve guideline adherence primarily by reducing potential undersurveillance. Conclusions This hybrid approach using open-weight large language models for structured extraction and guideline-encoded rules for decision-making can generate accurate, lightweight, and auditable postpolypectomy surveillance recommendations. Such a tool has the potential to improve safety netting and guideline adherence in NHS colonoscopy workflows.

items.title: INDUSTRIAL PRODUCT DESIGN IN THE AGE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: FRAMING THE NEED, SHAPING THE USE
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in physical products, from domestic appliances and vehicles to medical devices and wearables, yet the success of such products depends less on algorithmic performance than on whether people understand, trust and meaningfully integrate them into everyday life. This paper examines the contribution of industrial product design to the current need for, and use of, AI. Through a conceptual and integrative narrative review of literature in design research, human–computer interaction (HCI), computational design and AI ethics, it develops an analytical framework of five contributions: (1) framing human needs so that AI addresses problems worth solving; (2) making AI capabilities legible through form, interaction and feedback; (3) calibrating trust and control; (4) embedding AI in sustainable and ethical product lifecycles; and (5) integrating AI as a tool within the design process itself. The analysis indicates that industrial design acts as a mediating layer between technological capability and human practice, and that its contribution lies as much in deciding where AI should not be used as in enabling it. The paper closes with implications for practice, education and policy, and five propositions for empirical testing.

items.title: Influencer Marketing in The Age of Artificial Intelligence: Exploring The Impact Of Ai-Generated Influencers on Brand Credibility and Purchase Intention
items.abstract: Brands are increasingly partnering with AI-generated influencers — computer-generated personas that post, endorse, and interact on social media. Whether such endorsers can build the credibility on which purchase decisions depend remains unclear. This study examines the effect of five attributes of AI-generated influencers — Perceived Realism, Perceived Authenticity, Perceived Expertise, Parasocial Interaction, and Perceived Transparency (AI disclosure) — on Brand Credibility, and tests the role of Brand Credibility in shaping Purchase Intention.A descriptive and analytical research design was adopted, and primary data were collected from 400 social media users in Tamil Nadu who had encountered branded content from AI-generated influencers, using a structured five-point Likert-scale questionnaire and stratified random sampling by age group. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, multiple regression, and bootstrapped mediation analysis (PROCESS Model 4).All five attributes significantly predicted Brand Credibility, with Perceived Authenticity (β = 0.268) and Perceived Expertise (β = 0.206) strongest; the model explained 59.0% of its variance. Brand Credibility strongly predicted Purchase Intention (β = 0.424), and the full model explained 64.2% of the variance in intention. Brand Credibility significantly mediated all five relationships, fully for Perceived Realism and Perceived Transparency and partially for the others. The findings offer implications for brands, agencies, and regulators on the use and disclosure of AI-generated influencers

items.title: INNOVATIVE DIRECTIONS IN SOCIAL MEDIA MARKETING IN TOURISM: EVIDENCE, ATTRIBUTION, AND STRATEGIC ADOPTION
items.abstract: This article critically evaluates eight emerging directions in social media marketing for tourism and examines whether their growing practical adoption is supported by peer-reviewed empirical evidence. Particular attention is paid to the attribution gap between platform-level exposure and engagement metrics and subsequent tourism outcomes, including destination consideration, bookings, tourist expenditure, and post-visit advocacy. The study employs a structured literature review and conceptual analysis. Peer-reviewed research in tourism and hospitality, including recent systematic reviews, constitutes the primary evidence base. Official statistics, platform-reported data, and industry statistics are used exclusively to provide contextual information and are assessed according to the transparency of their sources. Assessments of adoption levels and evidence strength are explicitly analytical judgments rather than quantitatively measured scores. The reviewed evidence suggests a persistent imbalance between the adoption of marketing innovations and the demonstrated effects on tourism outcomes. User-generated content and electronic word of mouth have the strongest support for their underlying mechanisms among the eight directions examined, whereas influencer marketing, short-form video, social search, generative artificial intelligence, and other rapidly adopted practices are supported by varying levels of empirical evidence. The principal structural challenge concerns attribution: social media platforms effectively measure exposure and engagement, while economically meaningful tourism outcomes often occur at later stages, outside the platform environment, and without reliable data links to the initial exposure. The article approaches marketing innovation as an empirical proposition requiring evaluation rather than merely as an emerging trend to be adopted. It develops an evidence-graded assessment of eight innovative directions, proposes a three-tier strategic adoption framework—adopt now, pilot with measurement, and watch—and identifies a practical visitor-side measurement approach designed to help reduce the attribution gap between social media activities and tourism outcomes.

items.title: INTEGRATED COST-SCHEDULE AND PROCUREMENT ANALYTICS FOR CONSTRUCTION SUPPLY CHAINS IN SAUDI MEGA-PROJECTS: ENHANCING FORECASTING AND PROJECT DELIVERY UNDER VISION 2030
items.abstract: Saudi mega-projects operate through dense networks of designers, contractors, manufacturers, logistics providers and specialist suppliers, so cost and schedule performance cannot be governed effectively as separate reporting streams. Procurement commitments shape the timing and price of resources; schedule changes alter purchasing priorities and logistics demand; and commercial variations feed back into forecast completion cost. This review develops an integrated framework for cost-schedule and procurement analytics in construction supply chains, with particular relevance to Saudi Arabias Vision 2030 delivery environment. Thirty peer-reviewed studies published from 2020 to 2025 were synthesised across artificial intelligence in construction management, project cost prediction, schedule forecasting, construction supply-chain modelling, resilience and digital-twin-enabled control. The evidence indicates that predictive value emerges when cost, schedule and procurement records share consistent identifiers, timestamps and decision horizons. Machine-learning and hybrid models can improve forecasting, but isolated accuracy is insufficient unless outputs expose uncertainty, identify drivers and trigger accountable management action.

items.title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence and Multicenter Real-World Evidence to Advance Precision Dosing: A Critical Perspective Review
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Precision dosing integrates patient-specific factors to optimize pharmacotherapy. However, current evidence often relies on limited single-center studies, restricting generalizability. METHODS: A narrative review of literature on real-world evidence, pharmacogenetics, biomarkers, artificial intelligence (AI), and privacy-preserving data strategies relevant to precision dosing was conducted. RESULTS: Single-center data are insufficient for robust precision-dosing evidence because of small subgroups and local practice biases. Multicenter privacy-preserving systems enable richer, more generalizable datasets that link doses, exposures, genotypes, biomarkers, and outcomes. However, multicenter collaborations should remain aligned with the intended population and should not imply indiscriminate pooling of heterogeneous data. Secure pooled environments, federated learning, and synthetic data play distinct method-dependent roles. AI supports exposure estimation, phenotype extraction, and modeling of complex relationships but requires rigorous validation against conventional methods. Causal inference requires epidemiological rigor beyond predictive performance. CONCLUSIONS: Advancing precision dosing requires multicenter, purpose-specific, privacy-preserving, methodologically rigorous, and clinically validated data systems guided by clinical pharmacologists, with AI serving as a complementary tool rather than a default solution.

items.title: Integrating Generative AI Into an Undergraduate Research Methods Course: Evaluating Student Perceptions, AI Competency, and Intention to Use
items.abstract: College students increasingly use generative AI, yet formal undergraduate classroom implementation remains limited. This study evaluated a structured generative AI training in an undergraduate research methods course, examining its impact on students’ perceptions, self-rated competency, and future intention to use. Early in the semester, students received a lecture on generative AI tools, applications, and ethical issues, including bias, plagiarism, and data privacy. Two optional assignments provided hands-on practice using AI for literature searching and academic writing. After the course, 24 of 195 enrolled students completed a survey. Respondents reported low-to-moderate initial AI familiarity and competency. The lecture was well received and led to confidence in citing and disclosing AI use. Students expressed moderately positive intentions to use AI for future studying and research activities, while reporting concerns about accuracy and academic integrity. Findings suggest that structured, evidence-based AI training may support responsible use in undergraduates while addressing persistent ethical and practical concerns.

items.title: Integrating Situational Awareness Into Higher Education Curricula
items.abstract: Professional spaces today are rapidly changing, and to meet such swift changes in the environment, there is a rising demand for professionals who understand the dynamics of the place. They need human resources with the competence to perceive, interpret and respond effectively to the influx of their landscapes. Situational Awareness is a skill recognised in aviation, healthcare and domains that require quick responses to changing trajectories. However, it has not received significant attention in higher education despite its potential to develop professional competence and readiness. This article, thereby, aims to investigate the present gap in higher education curricula. It seeks to highlight understanding of situational awareness among the participants in the study, their perception of its need for professional success and the need to integrate it into higher education curricula. It emphasises the role of Situational Awareness in professional development and growth of an individual. The article endeavours to reason its crucial function in the learning phase of a student pursuing Higher Education and also aspires to rationalise its suitability as an important topic of perusal in the curriculum of Higher Education. It explores the vitality of the term and how it helps an individual fit in better in an environment. Personal interaction with the students helped us to analyse their understanding of the concept. In addition, a quantitative and cross-sectional survey design was undertaken for the present research. Data collection was based on structured online questionnaire in the format of six five-point Likert-scale items and demographic questions. The questionnaire incorporated aspects to measure participant's awareness of the term, its professional relevance, appropriate training of situational awareness in higher education, its contribution to boosting employability, whether it improves decision-making and the need for integration into higher education curricula. A sample of 72 participants, including undergraduates, postgraduate students, students with work experience and working professionals from engineering discipline with major emphasis, was used for the study. Descriptive and statistical techniques were deployed for the analysis of the data, particularly the aggregate percentage was taken for the scales reflecting agree and strongly agree parameters which was apparently higher than the neutral, disagree and strongly disagree parameters. The article relies on empirical evidence to assess participants’ perception of situational awareness as a vital skill in the present era. The results aim to inform the value and significance of situational awareness in developing professional competency for stakeholders, that is, curriculum developers, policymakers and higher education entities. The research aspires to contribute to repertoire of competence-based education by investigating as an important transferable skill to hone perception, adaptability and decision making of the students.

items.abstract: This article analyzes the possibilities and limits of Artificial Intelligence in organizing pedagogical evidence aimed at monitoring the learning pathways of students who are the target audience of Special Education. It develops a bibliographic and theoretical-conceptual study grounded in research on Artificial Intelligence and education, pedagogical documentation, mediating assessment, and Inclusive Special Education. It argues that Artificial Intelligence can contribute to systematizing records, integrating different sources of information, and expanding institutional pedagogical memory, but it cannot replace the ethical, relational, and interpretive processes carried out by teachers and pedagogical coordinators. The analysis indicates that data become evidence only when contextualized and interpreted in light of school experiences. It concludes that the contribution of Artificial Intelligence to democratic and inclusive education depends on its articulation with pedagogical documentation and human decisions committed to students’ singularities and to ensuring the right to learn.

items.title: Interpretable Dynamic Graph Learning via Dual‐Granularity Large Language Model Alignment
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Dynamic graph‐level embedding aims to learn whole‐graph representations from temporal snapshots. Existing methods predominantly follow a single‐vector paradigm that encodes each snapshot as a continuous latent vector, suffering from two key limitations: (1) Stage–Snapshot Entanglement, where within‐stage fluctuations and cross‐stage transitions are conflated without explicit granularity distinction; and (2) Implicit Structural Semantics, where meaningful structural properties remain buried in latent coordinates and are never exposed as interpretable, language‐compatible units. To address these issues, we propose DyGLLM, an LLM‐compatible framework that constructs and aligns dual‐granularity structural representations for dynamic graph understanding. Specifically, DyGLLM maps temporally coherent evolution regimes into selective structural tokens , providing explicit stage‐level anchors in the LLM token space. It further constructs graph fingerprints to verbalize each snapshot's prototype deviation, temporal variation and topological profile into language‐readable structural descriptions. A hybrid structure QA alignment mechanism with LoRA fine‐tuning is then introduced to align structural tokens and graph fingerprints with the LLM's representation space, enabling the model to interpret and reason over explicit structural contexts. Extensive experiments on five dynamic graph benchmarks demonstrate that DyGLLM achieves consistently competitive performance across graph similarity ranking, temporal anomaly detection and change point detection, validating the effectiveness of the proposed dual‐granularity structural representation.

items.title: InterviewAI: An Intelligent Virtual Interview Platform with Real-Time Voice, Video, and AI-Based Performance Evaluation
items.abstract: This paper presents InterviewAI, a Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) platform that conducts live mock interviews using artificial intelligence. Candidates often lack access to affordable and realistic interview practice, and existing systems either rely on static question banks or cover only parts of the interview experience. In InterviewAI, a user signs in with Google Authentication and uploads a resume in PDF format. The system extracts skills, education and experience, generates personalised questions, conducts the interview through real-time voice and video conversation with an AI interviewer, and produces a performance report covering strengths, weaknesses, communication skills and suggestions for improvement. A credit-based usage model with Razorpay payment integration makes the platform suitable for production use. The system is built on React.js, Node.js, Express.js and MongoDB, with Firebase authentication, Razorpay payments and OpenRouter for AI model access, and is deployed on Render. The platform was tried end to end with a few users to check its working, and all core modules, from sign-in to feedback report and payment, worked as intended.

items.title: Introduction
items.abstract: This introduction frames the book as both a personal reflection and a timely response to a rapidly changing world. Rooted in lived experience, it traces how the author’s journey through leadership, crisis, family life, entrepreneurship and inner development deepened the original framework of vocating beyond theory into practice. It also situates the book within a broader trilogy on leadership, business and capital as forces for good, with this edition focusing on how organisations can align purpose with structure, strategy and impact. A central new dimension is the recognition that artificial intelligence is reshaping not only work and learning, but also human identity, contribution and meaning. In response, the Introduction argues that vocation must be made more accessible and adaptive, especially for younger generations whose ways of engaging with knowledge are increasingly digital, interactive and fragmented. This conviction has led to the creation of Vocating.ai, a new venture designed to translate the Seven-Step Framework into a living, technology-enabled platform. The second book is therefore presented not simply as an update, but as a bridge between analogue wisdom and digital possibility in the enduring human search for purpose.

items.title: Investigating Pedestrian Safety Near Transit Bus Stops
items.abstract: This research examined how road and bus stop design and characteristics influence pedestrian safety, shaping both user perceptions and behaviors, and affecting crash outcomes near transit stops. A three-stage methodology integrated quantitative analysis with empirical field research. The first stage involved a macro-level quantitative analysis of factors contributing to pedestrian crashes, fusing together data on historical crash records, transit operations, demographic data, road inventories, and vehicle counts, and capturing over 300 crash-relevant features. Traditional and machine learning models were applied to classify bus stops and predict crash occurrence and severity. The second stage focused on human factors through a micro-level qualitative investigation, collecting public perceptions of safety through electronic surveys and comparing them with objective risk measures. The third stage consisted of systematic field observations documenting pedestrian behaviors and assessing how environmental and design characteristics influence these behaviors. By integrating objective crash modeling, subjective user perceptions, and observed behavior, the study developed a comprehensive framework for enhancing pedestrian safety. The findings inform actionable design guidelines and policy recommendations, supporting Vision Zero objectives and guiding transit agency standards, municipal complete streets policies, and national street design manuals.

items.title: IT Meets Academia: Giving Students the Tech Tools to Write the AI Rules
items.abstract: An AI administrator walks into an Honors English seminar. The assignment: prepare undergraduates to help write the course AI policy. This UNLV case study follows an unusual collaboration between a professor of postcolonial literature and the administrator of the university’s ChatGPT and Claude environments. The administrator also wrote UNLV’s draft institutional AI framework and experiences classroom AI rules as a PhD student. The session asks what becomes possible when the person who sees the systems behind the interface joins faculty and students in the policy conversation. Before students could write the rules, they needed enough technical literacy to understand what they were governing: model limitations, learning tradeoffs, differences between consumer and institutional accounts, data practices, authorship, transparency, and personal boundaries. The presenters will trace how that foundation prepared students to participate in course policy development. Dr. Beth Rosenberg will share why she invited IT into an English seminar, how students responded, and how the policy took shape. Attendees will leave with an adaptable model for combining IT knowledge, faculty expertise, and student agency to create AI expectations grounded in both technology and learning.

items.title: Keeping the patient's words: design of Aperta Health, a clinician-governed AI documentation-support prototype for multilingual and refugee mental health care in Australia
items.abstract: In the 2021 Census, 5.8 million people in Australia (22.8%) used a language other than English at home, and 872,000 said they spoke English not well or not at all. For people from refugee and migrant backgrounds, the first barrier to mental health care is often simply being understood. Services report that many clinicians do not engage interpreters, and when a consultation does cross languages, the patient's own words, idioms and explanations of distress are easily lost between the interpreter, the clinician and the record. Victoria's Royal Commission into its mental health system recommended developing digital technologies to deliver language services. This paper reports the design of Aperta Health, a web-based prototype that uses generative AI to help clinicians and bicultural workers turn multilingual or interpreter-mediated accounts into a structured, safety-conscious clinical record without discarding the original words. Its core design move is a strict division of labour. Deterministic code scores screening instruments and applies coded crisis rules. Generative AI only extracts, translates and drafts within bounded formats, and is told to write "Not stated in narrative" rather than invent findings. Qualified professionals interpret, diagnose, prescribe and escalate. We describe the design principles and architecture, then assess the prototype against Australian regulation. We conclude that several functions, including AI-drafted diagnostic formulations and public self-assessment, would be unlikely to qualify for the Therapeutic Goods Administration's exemption for clinical decision support software, and that the prototype's data flows do not yet meet the privacy expectations set out in national clinical AI guidance. We state these limits plainly. The prototype runs only on synthetic data, has not been clinically evaluated, and is not supplied for clinical use. The contribution is a reusable design pattern for language-inclusive mental health documentation, and an honest map of what stands between such a prototype and safe use. items.title: Key Data Analytics Trends to Explore Before Choosing a Data Analytics
items.abstract: Data analytics is changing how organisations operate, plan, and compete. Businesses use data to understand customer behaviour, improve services, reduce costs, and identify new opportunities. As digital systems expand, companies collect information from websites, applications, transactions, supply chains, and customer interactions. They need skilled professionals who can turn this information into clear and useful insights. At the same time, the field is evolving. Artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, cloud analytics, real-time reporting, and automated data preparation are changing how analysts work. These developments are creating new opportunities, but they also require learners to build strong foundations and keep their skills current. Choosing a Data Analytics Course in Ameerpet requires more than checking a course title. Learners should understand the current trends in the industry, the tools employers use, and the skills required for different career paths. This knowledge can help them select relevant training and prepare for the changing demands of the data analytics profession. The Growing Importance of Data Analytics Organisations no longer use data only to prepare monthly reports. They use it to support decisions across sales, finance, marketing, operations, healthcare, manufacturing, and technology. For example, a retailer can analyse sales records to forecast product demand. A bank can study transaction patterns to identify suspicious activity. A hospital can use operational reports to plan staff and resources. A marketing team can measure campaign performance to understand which activities produce results. These applications depend on accurate data, suitable analytical methods, and clear communication. Analysts must understand the business problem before selecting tools or drawing conclusions. The market outlook also reflects the growing role of analytics. Grand View Research estimated that India's data analytics market generated approximately US$4.23 billion in revenue in 2025 and projected that it could reach around US$47.51 billion by 2033. The forecast represents an estimated compound annual growth rate of 36.1% from 2026 to 2033. These are market projections, not guaranteed employment or salary outcomes. For learners considering a Data Analytics Course in Ameerpet, this growth highlights the value of developing practical skills that can be applied across industries. Artificial Intelligence and AI-Assisted Analytics Artificial intelligence is one of the most important trends in the analytics industry. AI tools can help analysts summarise datasets, identify patterns, generate queries, and automate routine tasks. This can reduce the time spent on some activities and allow professionals to focus more on interpreting results. For example, an analyst can use AI-assisted tools to explore sales performance or generate an initial summary of customer feedback. The analyst must still verify the output, check the data, and confirm that the conclusions are valid. In June 2026, Gartner identified AI-first operations, AI governance, and connected data and analytics platforms among the major trends shaping enterprise analytics. Its report also highlighted the need to manage the risks associated with AI-driven decisions. Learners should therefore understand both the benefits and the limits of AI. A Data Analytics Course in Ameerpet can provide a foundation in data analysis, while further learning can help students explore AI-assisted workflows. Important areas to understand include: Using AI tools to support data exploration. Checking AI-generated calculations and summaries. Understanding the basics of machine learning. Protecting confidential information when using AI systems. Applying human judgement to important business decisions. AI can support analytical work, but it does not remove the need for accurate data, sound reasoning, and accountability. Predictive and Prescriptive Analytics Traditional reporting often explains what has already happened. Predictive and prescriptive analytics extend this process by helping organisations estimate possible outcomes and assess potential actions. Predictive Analytics Predictive analytics uses historical data, statistical methods, and machine learning models to estimate future events. A retailer may forecast product demand from previous sales. A financial institution may estimate credit risk. A logistics company may use historical delivery information to identify the factors linked to delays. Learners should understand basic statistics, data preparation, and model evaluation before moving into advanced predictive techniques. Python and SQL can also support this work. Prescriptive Analytics Prescriptive analytics goes a step further by assessing possible actions based on defined objectives and constraints. For example, a supply chain team may use an optimisation model to assess delivery routes or inventory levels. Grand View Research identified predictive analytics as the largest segment of India's data analytics market by revenue in 2025, while its forecast identified prescriptive analytics as the fastest-growing type segment over the projection period. These developments show the value of understanding analytical methods beyond basic reporting. Learners considering a Data Analytics Course in Ameerpet should review whether the syllabus covers statistical reasoning and introduces advanced analytics at an appropriate level. Real-Time Data Analytics and Streaming Businesses increasingly need information as events occur. Real-time analytics helps teams monitor new data and respond to changes without waiting for a monthly or weekly report. For example, an e-commerce company can track order activity and inventory levels during a major sale. A transport company can monitor vehicle performance and delivery status. A financial organisation can use real-time systems to flag transactions that require further review. Real-time analytics often depends on data pipelines, cloud infrastructure, streaming technologies, and reliable monitoring systems. Entry-level analysts may not build these systems themselves, but an understanding of how data moves from source to dashboard can help them work more effectively with technical teams. A Data Analytics Course in Ameerpet should ideally teach learners the fundamentals of data collection, cleaning, and reporting before introducing more advanced real-time applications. Cloud Analytics and Modern Data Platforms Cloud analytics allows organisations to store, process, and analyse data through cloud-based services. It can help teams access information across locations and connect datasets from different business systems. Cloud platforms also support collaboration and scalable data processing. However, effective cloud analytics requires suitable access controls, cost management, data quality checks, and security practices. Modern data platforms increasingly bring together data engineering, analytics, governance, and AI capabilities. This creates a need for professionals who understand not only how to create a report but also where the data comes from and how it should be used. For beginners, the practical starting point is to understand spreadsheets, databases, SQL, data models, and visualisation tools. After building this foundation, learners can explore cloud data services and more advanced analytical workflows. Business Intelligence and Data Visualisation Business intelligence remains a key part of modern analytics. Organisations need clear dashboards and reports that help teams monitor performance and act on relevant findings. Tools such as Microsoft Power BI and Tableau help users present information through charts, tables, filters, and interactive dashboards. Excel remains useful for organising data and performing basic analysis. A well-designed dashboard can show revenue trends, customer retention, inventory levels, and operating costs in one place. The analyst must choose suitable metrics and explain their meaning without creating misleading impressions. A Data Analytics Course in Ameerpet that includes practical reporting exercises can help learners understand these concepts. When reviewing a programme, check whether it covers data preparation, dashboard design, data modelling, and the interpretation of business metrics. Data Quality, Privacy, and Responsible Analytics Advanced tools cannot compensate for poor-quality data. Missing values, duplicate records, incorrect formats, and inconsistent definitions can lead to inaccurate reports. Data quality and governance have become even more important as organisations expand their use of AI and self-service analytics. TechTarget's January 2026 review of business intelligence trends highlighted governance, data quality, and responsible access to analytics as important concerns for organisations. Learners should develop habits that support reliable analysis: Check the source and completeness of a dataset. Identify duplicate records and inconsistent values. Confirm that calculations use the correct definitions. Protect personal and confidential information. Document assumptions and limitations. Avoid drawing conclusions that the data cannot support. These practices apply to every industry. A Data Analytics Course in Ameerpet should help learners recognise that responsible data handling is part of professional analytics, not an optional extra. items.title: Large language model assistance for report-based carotid plaque AHA classification: a multi-reader study
items.abstract: Abstract Objectives To evaluate whether large language model assistance improves radiologists’ agreement with a text-based reference standard in inferring the modified American Heart Association carotid plaque classification from free-text MRI reports, and whether a lightweight model can perform well under criteria-guided prompting. Materials and methods This retrospective study included 433 patients from three institutions. In a report-based reader study, four radiologists classified MRI reports with and without large language model assistance. In standalone evaluation, a rule-based baseline and 10 models were compared under naive and criteria-guided prompting. The reference standard was expert consensus based on the report text. Results Among 433 patients (mean age, 65.9 years ± 13.4; 248 males), AI assistance improved six-class agreement with the text-based reference standard. At the vessel level, junior radiologists improved from 61.75% to 83.12% (Qwen3-8B) and 87.75% (DeepSeek-R1); senior radiologists from 77.00% to 87.50% and 92.25%, respectively (all Holm-corrected p < 0.001). Patient-level agreement increased from 41.0% to 78.8% (junior) and from 59.8% to 87.8% (senior) with DeepSeek-R1. Agreement increased (quadratic-weighted κ : 0.231 without AI vs 0.775 with DeepSeek-R1). In standalone evaluation, criteria-guided prompting improved Qwen3-8B agreement from 38.91% to 81.52% (95% CI: 78.87–84.06%), remaining 5.89 percentage points below DeepSeek-R1 (87.41%; 95% CI: 85.10–89.61%). Conclusion In this report-based classification setting, large language model assistance improved radiologists’ agreement with the text-based reference standard, with larger gains in junior radiologists. When prompts explicitly encoded AHA criteria, an 8B local candidate model performed well, supporting its potential use as a standardization aid for text-based workflows. Key Points Question Report-based modified AHA classification of carotid plaques is experience-dependent and difficult to standardize, as mapping multi-sequence imaging findings to classification conclusions imposes substantial cognitive load. Findings Large language model assistance improved agreement with a text-based reference standard and raised inter-reader consistency (weighted κ 0.231–0.775), narrowing the junior–senior gap. Critical relevance statement Embedding explicit AHA criteria in the prompt let an 8B model approach 671B-model agreement (38.91–81.52%), supporting standardized text-based workflows without fine-tuning.

items.title: Latent profiles of work readiness and their associated factors among nursing interns: a cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Background Work readiness refers to the comprehensive competencies required for individuals to enter and adapt to the workforce. It is relevant to the transition from nursing student to clinical nurse. However, existing research has paid limited attention to heterogeneity in nursing interns’ work readiness, and few studies have examined associated factors from the perspective of Social Cognitive Career Theory. This study aimed to identify latent profiles of work readiness among nursing interns and examine the associations of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) literacy and the clinical learning environment with profile membership. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted among 712 final-year nursing interns from three nursing schools in Anhui Province, China, between November 2025 and June 2026. Participants completed the Nursing Practice Readiness Scale, Clinical Learning Environment Questionnaire, and Generative Artificial Intelligence Literacy Scale. Latent Profile Analysis was used to identify distinct work readiness profiles, and multinomial logistic regression was performed to examine factors associated with profile membership. Results Three latent profiles of work readiness were identified: low work readiness ( n = 415, 58.3%), moderate work readiness ( n = 227, 31.9%), and high work readiness ( n = 70, 9.8%). The overall multinomial logistic regression model( χ 2 = 467.253, P < 0.001) showed that the clinical learning environment, GenAI literacy, academic performance, clinical learning outcomes, and sense of professional belonging were significantly associated with work readiness profile membership (all P < 0.05). Conclusions Three distinct work readiness profiles were identified among nursing interns. Clinical learning environment, GenAI literacy, academic performance, clinical learning outcomes, and sense of professional belonging were associated with profile membership. These findings highlight the heterogeneity of nursing interns’ work readiness and may inform the development of individualized educational support strategies.

items.title: Lecture Theatre Rehabilitation and Classroom Seating Capacity Expansion Project
items.abstract: Executive Overview This document presents an independent institutional infrastructure proposal titled “Lecture Theatre Rehabilitation and Classroom Seating Capacity Expansion Project," developed as a turnkey capital intervention model for Kaduna Polytechnic, Kaduna State, Nigeria. Designed to eliminate severe classroom congestion and safety hazards resulting from shortages of functional furniture, this proposal establishes a comprehensive framework for modernizing lecture halls, refurbishing civil structures, and deploying heavy-duty, ergonomic student seating across central academic complexes. Technical Scope & Infrastructure Pillars The proposed intervention covers four primary spatial and structural pillars: 1. Civil & Architectural Refurbishment: Complete floor leveling, acoustic ceiling repairs, wall re-plastering/painting, and lighting restoration across major central lecture halls and auditoriums. 2. Furniture Procurement & Capacity Expansion: Design, local fabrication, and installation of durable, dual-seat metal-frame desk units and fixed auditorium seating to accommodate over 4,000 students simultaneously. 3. Safety & Universal Design Compliance: Re-configuration of seating layouts to adhere to international emergency egress standards, wider gangways, and dedicated accessible seating areas for students with mobility impairments. 4. Maintenance & Asset Tracking System: Implementation of institutional asset-tagging and a preventative maintenance schedule to protect public physical infrastructure from rapid wear and degradation. Financial Framework & Project Metrics · Proposed Beneficiary Institution: Kaduna Polytechnic, Kaduna State, Nigeria · Target Supervising Units: Directorate of Works and Physical Planning & School Deans / Academic Board · Implementation Duration: 6 Months · Total Estimated Budget: ₦107,697,500 NGN (Approx. $81,000 USD at interbank rates) · Target Funding Mechanism: OPEC Fund for International Development (OFID) – Public Sector Operations Grant / Loan Facility. Purpose & Open-Access Availability This document is published on Zenodo as an open-access policy and educational facilities engineering model. It serves as an actionable benchmark for university administrators, social infrastructure planners, educational policy researchers, and multilateral funding agencies seeking structured templates for classroom capacity expansion in developing economies.

items.title: Legal Approaches to Deepfakes: Contextualising India’s Intermediary Guidelines Amendments in the Global Regulatory Environment
items.abstract: The article examines India’s 2026 amendments to the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules in relation to synthetically generated information, covering deepfake creation and distribution. It first identifies the need for regulation in India, drawing on recent instances of deepfake-related events, and then places those needs in a comparative perspective by analysing regulatory approaches in China, the European Union and the United States. The article argues that India has adopted a hybrid intermediary-liability model that combines labelling, provenance, technical-prevention, user-declaration and accelerated takedown obligations while still relying on existing criminal, electoral, consumer-protection, privacy and personality-rights frameworks to do much of the hard work. By situating India’s framework within the broader global regulatory environment, the article contributes to current debates on how legal systems should respond to harmful synthetic media without unduly constraining other beneficial uses of generative AI. Overall, the analysis shows that India’s Intermediary Guidelines Amendments offer a reasonable response to the main issues at stake but leave considerable room for other areas of law to do the heavy lifting. The article concludes on a cautionary note, highlighting the expected challenges of future implementation.

items.title: Liability at the Authority Boundary: A Framework for Allocating Responsibility Across Distributed and Agentic AI Systems
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly deployed through systems in which authority, execution, oversight, and consequence no longer belong to the same actor. A model may be developed by one organization, integrated by another, configured by an enterprise, instructed by a human, executed through an AI agent, routed through external tools, and experienced by a person who had no role in any of those decisions. The resulting liability problem is not adequately described by asking whether a human remained "in the loop" or whether an audit trail exists. This working paper develops the GAILC Authority Boundary framework. It defines the Authority Boundary as the point at which consequential decision rights, discretion, intervention responsibility, or consequence-bearing responsibility passes from one actor, system, organization, or layer to another, and analyses each boundary through five elements: Authority, Transfer, Reliance, Intervention, and Consequence. The framework identifies two difficult liability cases that conventional control models often leave unresolved. Intended-Execution Liability concerns harm produced when a system remains within its authority, follows policy, uses permitted tools, and operates substantially as designed. No-Action Liability concerns harm produced or worsened where an actor bears an identifiable duty or assigned responsibility to act, possesses the authority, information, timing, and practical capacity to do so, yet no consequential intervention occurs. The paper introduces the Authority Envelope, the distinction between authorization and judgment, the Silence-as-Authority Problem, the GAILC Allocation Test, Consequence Ownership, Allocation Completeness and Allocation Adequacy, Residual Consequence, and Orphaned Harm. It proposes a standardized Authority Boundary Record (ABR) designed to support verification, contestability, and independent adjudication, together with a boundary failure taxonomy, an irreversibility threshold, an inter-organizational allocation procedure, and a pre-deployment test. Its central proposition is that traceability is evidence, not allocation: an authority and execution chain may be fully reconstructable while accountability and consequence allocation remain incomplete. The framework is analytical and does not determine legal liability. It is positioned in relation to agency law, duties concerning failures to act, design-defect analysis, and scholarship on the problem of many hands, responsibility gaps, and moral crumple zones. This paper is the third in the GAILC Working Paper series, following WP001 (The Human Presence Economy) and WP002 (The Intervention Test).

items.title: Life Cycle Assessment of Activated TIG Welding: Energy and Environmental Trade-offs in an Iranian Case Study with Sensitivity Analysis
items.abstract: Abstract Welding efficiency and environmental performance are critical in industrial applications. This study presents a cradle to gate life cycle assessment (LCA) comparing conventional tungsten inert gas (TIG) welding with activated tungsten inert gas (A-TIG) welding for producing 100 mm bead-on-plate welds on grade 304L stainless steel. In A TIG, a TiO₂ methanol flux allows a lower welding current while achieving a comparable penetration depth. Calculated welding electricity consumption, measured flux-preparation electricity consumption, and material inputs were modeled in SimaPro 9.2 using Ecoinvent 3 datasets. Midpoint impacts were assessed using the EPD 2018 method, and endpoint impacts were assessed using ReCiPe 2016 Hierarchist method. Results show that A-TIG reduced welding electricity consumption by approximately 40% compared with TIG and yielded lower modeled acidification, eutrophication, and global warming potentials. Water scarcity impacts were nearly identical for the two processes. However, However, A-TIG’s normalized photochemical ozone creation potential (POCP) score was 68.1 percentage points higher than TIG’s, with the higher impact set to 100% in each category, primarily because of modeled methanol emissions and upstream flux-production impacts. A one-at-a-time sensitivity analysis covering 30 scenarios showed that the comparative ranking of the two processes remained unchanged within the investigated parameter ranges, with methanol mass identified as the dominant influence on POCP. Endpoint modeling indicated that the human-health category dominated the weighted damage profile. These results represent potential life-cycle impacts rather than measured occupational health effects. This experimental cradle-to-gate LCA of penetration-matched bead-on-plate welding indicates that flux-assisted welding can reduce several impacts associated with electricity consumption while introducing trade-offs related to photochemical ozone creation. These findings support the optimization of activating flux formulations and welding parameters within the investigated conditions, while their applicability to industrial joints requires further validation.

items.title: Machine Learning & Artificial Intelligence in the Development of Gastro-Retentive Drug Delivery Systems: Current Advances & Future Prospectives
items.abstract: The integration of machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) into pharmaceutical sciences is reshaping the development of advanced drug delivery systems. Traditional gastroprotective drug delivery systems (GRDDS) are designed to prolong the residence time of oral dosage forms in the stomach to enhance bioavailability and therapeutic efficacy for drugs with narrow absorption windows. However, conventional formulation development often relies on empirical optimization, which is time-consuming and resource-intensive. AI and ML bring a data-driven paradigm to this complex landscape by enabling computational modeling, predictive analytics, and intelligent optimization of formulation parameters. These technologies can analyze multidimensional datasets to identify patterns and relationships between formulation components, physiological variables, and release kinetics that would be challenging to discern using traditional methods. AI-assisted models such as artificial neural networks, support vector machines, and Bayesian optimization have demonstrated significant potential in predicting drug release profiles, selecting optimal polymer systems, and simulating gastric behavior. Moreover, AI can streamline experimental design, reduce trial-anderror iterations, and accelerate the development timeline, thus improving formulation robustness and performance. The convergence of AI with gastroprotective systems also promises personalized approaches that account for patient-specific gastric motility and physiological factors, fostering tailored therapies. Although challenges remain—such as the need for high-quality datasets, interpretability of complex models, and integration with regulatory frameworks—the current advances provide a compelling foundation for future research. Embracing these intelligent tools in GRDDS development is likely to expand the frontiers of oral drug delivery by enhancing design precision, improving therapeutic outcomes, and reducing developmental costs. Continued innovation and interdisciplinary collaboration will be essential to fully harness the transformative potential of AI and ML in pharmaceutics.

items.title: Machine Learning in Hand Pathology Diagnosis: A Narrative Review of Current Insights
items.abstract: Machine learning (ML), a subset of artificial intelligence (AI), is revolutionizing health care. Given the intricate anatomy and functional complexity of the hand, AI applications in hand pathology are gaining prominence, particularly in the diagnosis of fractures, nerve injuries, and musculoskeletal disorders. This review summarizes ML advancements in hand pathology diagnosis, enhancing clinical history analysis, examination findings interpretation, and imaging assessment. A systematic search of PubMed, Google Scholar, EMBASE, Cochrane CENTRAL, Scopus, and Web of Science from 1901 to March 2025 was conducted, focusing on ML applications in diagnosing hand fractures, tendon injuries, and nerve compressions. The inclusion criteria encompassed original research, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and observational studies that demonstrated the use of AI in diagnostic imaging, preoperative assessment, or postoperative management. Studies that did not involve AI-driven diagnostic applications or lacked sufficient methodological transparency were excluded. Machine learning models, particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs), have demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy in detecting fractures. Studies have validated CNNs in the detection of distal radius and ulna fractures, outperforming trainees and urgent care physicians. In addition, AI has enhanced clinical examination by integrating wearable motion sensors for objective joint assessment. However, challenges such as external validation, interpretability, and integration into clinical workflows remain, limiting broader clinical adoption. Machine learning shows promise in hand pathology diagnosis, but widespread adoption requires improved external validation, standardized methods, and interdisciplinary collaboration. Future research should prioritize multicentric studies and explainable AI to enhance trust and integration.

items.title: Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and IoT for Waste Classification and Intelligent Waste Management: A PRISMA-Based Systematic Review
items.abstract: The rapid growth of urban populations and consumption patterns has significantly increased the volume and complexity of municipal waste streams, including recyclable, organic, hazardous, and electronic waste. Traditional waste management approaches such as manual sorting and fixed collection schedules struggle to handle the diversity and scale of modern waste systems efficiently. Consequently, recent research has explored artificial intelligence (AI), computer vision, and Internet of Things (IoT) technologies to automate waste classification and enable intelligent monitoring and management of waste infrastructures. However, the rapidly expanding literature in this domain is fragmented across different datasets, sensing platforms, and experimental settings, making it difficult to obtain a comprehensive understanding of current technological progress. To address this gap, this study conducts a systematic literature review using the PRISMA methodology, analyzing 50 rigorously selected peer-reviewed studies on automated waste classification and intelligent waste management systems. The protocol was registered in the Open Science Framework (OSF). The reviewed works are examined in terms of model architectures, sensing infrastructures, datasets, and system capabilities. The analysis shows that convolutional neural network architectures such as ResNet, MobileNet, and EfficientNet, together with object detection frameworks including YOLO and Faster R-CNN, dominate current visual waste classification research; however, emerging studies increasingly explore hybrid architectures combining convolutional networks with transformer-based models to improve contextual understanding and scalability. IoT-enabled smart bins equipped with ultrasonic sensors, load cells, and environmental sensors are widely used for real-time waste monitoring. The review also reveals a recent surge of research activity, particularly in Asia, with increasing contributions from major publishers such as Elsevier and MDPI. Despite promising experimental performance, most systems remain limited to small curated datasets and pilot-scale deployments, highlighting a gap between laboratory research and real-world implementation. These findings provide a consolidated overview of current research trends and identify key challenges for developing scalable and practical intelligent waste management systems.

items.title: Malfunction Reporting Patterns in Life-Supporting Versus Noninvasive Ventilators: A Stratified Text-Mining Analysis of the FDA Device MAUDE Database
items.abstract: Background: Mechanical ventilators are essential life-support devices, yet evidence regarding device-related vulnerabilities remains limited compared with the extensive literature on human-factor–related adverse events. This study applied text-mining techniques to a large post-market surveillance database to examine ventilator malfunction reporting patterns and the effect of stratifying reports by device category. Methods: Adverse event reports related to mechanical ventilators submitted to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration’s Manufacturer and User Facility Device Experience database between January 2010 and December 2025 were stratified into life-supporting and noninvasive devices and analyzed using KH Coder. A random sample of the life-supporting reports was drawn for the primary analysis. Frequency analysis, co-occurrence network analysis, hierarchical cluster analysis, and correspondence analysis were performed. Device brand and year were used as external variables in the correspondence analysis. Results: A total of 193,926 reports met the eligibility criteria, of which 177,641 were classified as malfunctions. The analyses were restricted to reports classified as malfunctions. Among life-supporting ventilators, the reported malfunctions spanned several broad themes, including power and battery failures, circuit-board and electronic faults, breathing-circuit and gas-delivery problems, and issues involving monitoring and control functions. Among noninvasive devices, reports were concentrated in terms associated with a single foam-related recall, as well as connector corrosion and patient-reported symptoms. Nearly 1 in 5 malfunction reports did not document a confirmed device failure during patient use. Conclusions: Text mining of ventilator-related adverse event reports revealed distinct reporting patterns across life-supporting and noninvasive devices. These findings are exploratory and do not establish the frequency or causes of device failure. Stratification of reports by device category helped prevent the reporting patterns of individual devices from being obscured by a single recall. This study demonstrates the potential value of combining post-market surveillance data with text-mining methods to support medical device safety surveillance.

items.title: Managerial Readiness for Artificial Intelligence in Textile Wastewater Management in Bangladesh
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence offers potential applications in wastewater monitoring, prediction, and operational decision support. However, selecting a model does not establish that factory managers and treatment operators can use it effectively. This conceptual article examines managerial readiness for artificial intelligence in Bangladesh's textile wastewater management. It brings together selected literature on organizational readiness, artificial intelligence capabilities, and wastewater applications, alongside Bangladesh-specific research and institutional reports. The article proposes six readiness domains: strategic commitment, managerial and operator knowledge, data stewardship, operational integration, investment and partnership capacity, and accountable decision making. It further distinguishes exploratory interest, supervised experimentation, routine decision support, and controlled operational integration as different adoption states. Four propositions explain how readiness may influence movement between these states and the translation of adoption into environmental performance. A proposed qualitative multiple-case design specifies evidence needed to examine these propositions, including decision histories, operational records, interviews across organizational levels, and observations of treatment routines. The framework is an analytical proposal rather than a validated measurement scale or report of completed fieldwork. Its contribution is to connect organizational preparation with the specific decisions, responsibilities, and verification practices required for textile wastewater management. Empirical research is needed to assess its relevance across factories with different resources and treatment arrangements.

items.title: Managing quality-oriented big data: a conceptual architecture for acquisition, fusion, and analytics in data-driven organizations
items.abstract: Data-driven organizations increasingly depend on large, heterogeneous, and fast-moving data to sustain the quality of their products, services, and processes. The transition toward data-driven organizational quality, often discussed under the label of Quality 4.0, has so far been examined mainly through a managerial lens. As a result, the data foundations of that transition remain fragmented and under-theorized. This Conceptual Analysis reframes quality-oriented big data as a first-class data management problem and proposes a layered conceptual architecture that organizes the lifecycle of such data across five interconnected layers: multi-source acquisition, integration and fusion, data quality assurance, analytics and knowledge extraction, and data governance and ethics. The central argument is that data quality operates as a central mediating construct linking big data capability to organizational quality outcomes: analytics improves organizational quality in large part to the extent that the underlying data are accurate, complete, consistent, timely, and well governed. Drawing on the data management, data quality, and machine learning systems literatures, the article specifies the constituent elements of each layer, the dependencies among them, and the failure modes that arise when the data foundation is neglected. Five propositions and a structured research agenda position the acquisition, fusion, quality assurance, and governance of quality-oriented big data as priorities for data mining and management research. The architecture offers a data-centric vocabulary for designing and evaluating the data infrastructures on which data-driven organizational quality ultimately depends.

items.title: Mapping knowledge management in Industry 4.0 era: a TCCM-guided bibliometric and thematic analysis
items.abstract: This study systematically maps and synthesizes the evolving literature on knowledge management (KM) in the context of Industry 4.0 (I4.0) by integrating bibliometric analysis with the Theory-Context-Characteristics-Method (TCCM) framework. Drawing on 93 peer-reviewed articles from Scopus (2018–2025), the study employs Biblioshiny and VOSviewer to analyze publication trends, intellectual structures, and thematic development, complemented by a structured TCCM-based synthesis. The findings reveal arapidly growing yet uneven field, dominated by perspectives on dynamic capabilities and absorptive capacity, with astrong concentration in manufacturing contexts and developed economies. Methodologically, the literature relies heavily on cross-sectional survey designs, while computational and longitudinal approaches remain limited. Thematic analysis identifies digital transformation, knowledge sharing, and organizational learning as core areas, whereas artificial intelligence, knowledge transfer, and governance remain underdeveloped. To address these gaps, the study proposes the Dynamic Knowledge Management Capability (DKMC) framework, conceptualizing KM as a technology-mediated capability shaped by human-AI interaction, real-time knowledge flows, and governance mechanisms. The study provides a transparent, theory-integrated synthesis and contributes to KM scholarship by incorporating AI-mediated knowledge processes and governance considerations, offering directions for future research and practice in digitally intensive environments.

items.title: Mapping the Research Landscape of Artificial Intelligence and Lifelong Learning: A Scientometric Analysis Using ScientoPy
items.abstract: The convergence of artificial intelligence (AI) and lifelong learning has attracted growing educational, computational, and policy attention, yet its intellectual structure has not been mapped systematically. This study reports a scientometric analysis of the AI-lifelong learning literature indexed in Scopus and the Web of Science Core Collection between 2014 and 2024. Records retrieved from both databases (N = 347) were merged and duplicated in ScientoPy, yielding 259 unique documents. Research momentum was quantified with three time-normalized indicators, average growth rate (AGR), average documents per year (ADY), and percentage of documents published in the last years (PDLY), across six analytical dimensions. Output grew from one document in 2014 to 116 in 2024; across the five principal document types (n = 220), 70.5% of records appeared in 2023-2024. Conference papers (41.3%) and journal articles (38.2%) predominated, with articles expanding fastest (AGR = 21.5; PDLY = 71.7%). Education & Educational Research recorded the highest normalized momentum among subject categories (AGR = 7.0; PDLY = 89.5%). Lifelong learning (n = 57) and artificial intelligence (n = 53) anchored the keyword field, while ChatGPT and Higher Education emerged entirely within the final two years. The United States led in volume (n = 57), whereas India (n = 29; PDLY = 89.7%) showed the strongest recent acceleration. Triangulating these indicators suggests, as an interpretive inference rather than a network-based measurement, that the corpus comprises three largely separate epistemic communities sharing a label but not a research program, framing an agenda for integrative, ethically grounded scholarship.

items.title: Measuring Organizational Constructs in Large-Scale Text: An interpretive framework combining topic modeling and BERT
items.abstract: Measuring organizational constructs in large-scale unstructured text requires methods that preserve interpretive depth while enabling systematic, per-document classification. Structural Topic Modeling (STM) supports interpretive depth by surfacing patterns that inform construct operationalization, but its topic proportions are not designed as standalone per-document construct measures; transformer-based models such as BERT can scale measurement but require construct operationalization grounded in interpretive work. We address this challenge through a two-stage framework in which STM and BERT play structurally distinct roles. Coding schemes are developed through qualitative interpretation and STM analysis; BERT is then fine-tuned to apply these schemes across documents. We formalize two research approaches—construct-guided and pattern-discovery—that provide principled paths from different theoretical starting points toward a shared methodological endpoint: validated, auditable per-document construct measures. We illustrate the framework using more than 20,000 employee reviews. The framework supports iterative construct validation, using computational diagnostics to guide interpretive refinement and producing document-level measures suitable for theory-informed organizational analysis.
